loop: Drafting, reviewing and refining the ShipCAD app root spec.
worked: Two read-only architect reviews caught concrete gaps in SVG input safety, cockpit identity, local versus portable state, handoff, and game bundle isolation.
The spec stayed within the requested line budget and passed the spec check after the user clarified ownership and verified the result.

issues.observation: I treated the /lab/ URL prefix as evidence that the Game Dev Lab hosted ShipCAD, then dropped the prefix when app ownership was corrected.
issues.effect: The user had to clarify ownership and URL conventions separately.
issues.interpretation: I conflated the route namespace with both app ownership and the Astro host boundary.

issues.observation: The physical layout and Design System dependency were not explicit at first; I then suggested a separate UI package before the user chose one ShipCAD package.
issues.effect: The architecture took additional turns to settle, and Design System extraction remains separate from this spec.
issues.interpretation: A table of concrete paths and dependency directions earlier would have exposed the missing decisions sooner.

issues.observation: The user considered most scenarios better suited to child specs, but provisionally approved them while those specs do not exist.
issues.effect: The root keeps those scenarios for now; their placement should be revisited when child specs exist.
issues.interpretation: I prioritized preserving draft behavior over keeping every scenario strictly at app level.
